rejected.title: Bringing Them Home and the Apology
card: From about 1910 to 1970, governments and church missions took many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families. These children are known as the Stolen Generations.
A national inquiry heard the stories of hundreds of people who had been removed. Its report, Bringing Them Home, was released in 1997.
The report found that removal caused lasting harm, including the loss of family, language, culture and Country. It recommended apologies.
On 13 February 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologised in Parliament, on behalf of the nation, for the laws and policies that caused this harm.
rejected.remember: The 1997 report recorded the harm, and the nation apologised for it in 2008.

a.q: How was the Bringing Them Home report linked to the 2008 Apology?
opts: It recorded the harm and called for apologies
It was the speech given at the 2008 Apology
It ended removals that were still going on in 2008
It returned land to the Stolen Generations
a.why: The report recorded the stories and the harm of removal in 1997, and it recommended apologies. The Apology was a separate speech in Parliament, eleven years later.
a.clue: Which came first, the report or the Apology?

b.q: Uncle Ray was taken from his family as a child in the 1950s, and later told his story to the national inquiry. In 2008 he watches the Apology. What did the Apology say sorry for?
opts: Laws and policies that removed children
The time it took to release the 1997 report
Only removals carried out by church missions
Removals that took place after the Apology
b.why: The Apology said sorry, on behalf of the nation, for the laws and policies that removed children like Ray. It was not limited to church missions, since governments carried out removals too.
b.clue: Who made the laws and policies that removed children?
